synthesis.overnight_summary: Gold faded into Friday's MCX close as Brent's spike to ~$110 (five-month high) lifted the US 10Y to ~5.11%, leaving spot ~$4,163 at 00:51 IST and ending the week ~0.7% lower near $4,165. Over the weekend Hormuz attacks continued (supertanker mine strike, tug hit, 10 ships in a week) and the Saudi-Houthi war escalated, while Trump's waiver of Russia sanctions pulled Brent back to ~$108 in Asia. Monday's open is supportive: Treasury yields extended their biggest weekly drop in eight months (10Y 5.06%) on AI-debt jitters that sank Nikkei 2% and Kospi 1.6%, and FedWatch October hold odds rose to ~84%, pushing spot to ~$4,173-4,181. The rupee is seen flat near 94.95, so the model fair open is ~Rs 148273 (+Rs 355) - a modest gap-up driven by COMEX alone; the first MCX print of 148,397 sits Rs 124 above it, inside the Rs 300 band. With Tuesday's morning session shut for Dussehra and no Fed speakers until 28-Oct, MCX should trade off spot, yields and Gulf headlines, with $4,185-4,200 the cap.
